# Document Clause

A root-local clause for preparing and embedding one document, either by constructing it from configured inputs or accepting an existing initialized publication from a supplier. It tracks preparation, selection and usability separately. Its exact type adds no domain-specific terms, candidate restrictions or follow-up actions beyond the inherited preparation checks.

## Configuration and inputs

- `bindings.document` is the destination pointer and embedded-document location. `cardinality` is `single`; preparation `key` defaults to `single` and cannot have another value.
- `bindings.parties` is the party-mapping object. It defaults to `{}`, but preparation requires a nonempty mapping. `bindings.sources` is the source-mapping object and defaults to `{}`.
- `bindings.template` is an optional, snapshotted template pointer. Source-validator planning uses `parameters.template` when present, otherwise the template snapshot. No default pointer paths are established.
- Parameters are read from the document. `obtain` defaults to `create`; only `create` and `provide` are accepted. `create` rejects a nonempty `suppliedParties` list. `provide` requires nonempty `suppliedBy`, which identifies the supplier channel.
- Preparation accepts `fields` and `values`, each defaulting to `{}` and constrained by the configured template. `requestId` defaults to the resolved `key` and must be nonempty text.
- `specialization/dataPaths` defaults to `[]`. Its entries designate existing data slots that a supplied document may specialize. Paths must be absolute, nonoverlapping and outside reserved roots: `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `sources`, `type`, `blueId`, `instanceKey`, `creationIntent` and `preparationContext`.

Source declarations are collected from the template’s `sources` and its clauses’ `parameters.sources`. Conflicting declarations for the same alias are rejected; generated matching checks reject undeclared aliases and test declared sources against their constraints.

## Preparation and provision

`prepare` checks the mapping, singleton key, request identifier and destination. An existing entry with different preparation intent is rejected; matching intent is classified as `duplicate` during checking. Intent includes configuration, template, `fields`, `values` and `requestId`. Without an existing entry, an occupied destination is rejected.

Preparation constructs the document, configures sources and records `prepared`, `slots`, `domainTerms` and `requirementRef`, identifying the exact prepared requirement. It emits `Document Prepared` with `clauseId`, `itemKey`, `requestId`, `requirementRef` and `status`.

With `obtain: create`, it writes the prepared document to `bindings.document` and records `documentOrigin` and `status: selected`. With `obtain: provide`, it records `status: awaiting_provider` and emits `Document Provision Requested`, identifying `party`, `inResponseTo`, `itemKey`, `clauseId` and `requirementRef`. This request does not confirm that a document has been supplied or become usable.

`provide` accepts `document`, an existing initialized publication reference, plus `inResponseTo` and `requirementRef`; `key` defaults to `single`. It requires an existing preparation in `provide` mode, the exact supplier channel, and matching request and requirement references. Provision is rejected in `reapproval_required`, `admission_denied`, `cancelled` or `cancellation_requested` status.

The candidate’s initialized original must match the prepared document after permitted slots are normalized, and its effective clause policy must remain consistent. Slot values must satisfy their declarations. Specialized data must remain unchanged between the initialized original and current publication. Party checks require consistent main-party identity, preserve nonsupplied parties, reject undeclared parties and preserve the required approval policy. A previously selected origin cannot be replaced with a different origin.

A validated candidate may still require admission: a stage other than `ready` updates the preparation record and emits `Document Admission Progress` without selecting the destination. A `ready` candidate is written to the destination as a reference, recorded as `selected`, and reported through `Document Selected`. Selection is not confirmation of usability.

## State, refresh and cancellation

Preparation state is initialized at `/process_<clauseKey>` with `entries: {}`. Entries record `key`, `requestId`, destination `path`, their own `itemPath`, preparation intent, supplier, requirement, selected origin and `status`. These paths belong to the document executing the clause, including when that document is nested. Missing state does not establish completion or a default status.

`resume`, destination updates and embedded-node notifications invoke refresh. For a selected document with `/contracts/initialized/document`, refresh verifies that its origin still matches `documentOrigin`. It sets `usable` only when that document’s `/activation/active` is exactly `true` and `namedSourcesReady` succeeds; otherwise it sets `selected`. Entering `usable` emits `Document Attached`. Usability can revert to `selected`. Missing initialization does not establish readiness. This exact type produces no domain `nextActions`.

`cancel` requires an existing preparation without `documentOrigin`; selected documents require domain cancellation instead. It sets `cancellation_requested` and emits `Preparation Cancellation Requested`. Repeating that request returns `duplicate`. Neither the status nor the event confirms completed cancellation.

## Admission and access

When activation parameters contain nonempty `admission/approvers`, each approver must be a distinct declared party. Admission state includes `editable`, `grants`, `retired` and a `ledger` initialized with revision `1`, empty history and empty proposal. Approvals identify an existing `proposalId`, require an authorized approver channel and `call/requireExactDocumentVersion: true`, and apply the proposed grants only after every configured approver approves. Stale or changed proposals, frozen editing and conflicting identifiers are rejected; repeated approvals are recognized as duplicates. Rebase requests identify `admissionRef`, with singleton `key` defaulting to `single`.

Each activation party receives an access-registration operation accepting `documents`: one to sixteen existing initialized Timeline Access publications. Registration is described as checking initialization, authority and permitted access, and is followed by activation refresh. Access documents are embedded under `/processAccess_<clauseKey>`. Available operations do not establish the current viewer’s authorization or personal obligation.

The preparation transition hook rejects changes with `PREPARATION_IMMUTABLE_WHILE_OBLIGATIONS_EXIST`. The supplied definitions do not expose the full construction, admission-staging, access-registration or named-source-readiness rules; their exact additional checks remain unspecified here.
